_note: Newest first, one entry per big update with at most five lines that sum it up. The top version must match MARKETING_VERSION in project.yml (tools/check_content.py checks): a small change moves the top entry's version and date along and adds a line only if it's big enough to tell players. 1.0.0 is the App Store release.

releases.title: Waystones and favours
notes: Seven waystones out in the wild wake when you finish their quests: touch one to travel free to any town you've been to or waystone you've woken, and Homeward Feathers and Bridge of Light reach them too.
Some quests are favours now: carry something to someone in another land, and bring back what they send.
Elite quests ask more of you for bigger rewards, and every quest shows how hard it is, from Easy to Elite.

Every land builds its own homes now: adobe houses and tents in the desert, beach huts by the sea, snowy cabins and an igloo in the north, stilt huts in the swamps and crooked cottages where it's spooky.
Heroes hold their weapon upright at their side when they face you, and a whip's lash hangs down to their feet.

releases.title: Hats of their own
notes: Every helmet, hood, coif and wizard's hat is a hat of its own now, worn in the Hat slot: one for each armour, in its colour, sold, dropped and given wherever the armour is.
An armour and its hat together are worth what the armour was, and the hats for the armour you already have are waiting in your bag.
A barber in every town gives you a new hairstyle and hair colour, for 1000 gold.
The world map shows who's where in the lands you've been to, and bats keep to their own lands.

releases.title: Into the deep
notes: The Glimmerdeep goes two levels deeper, down ladders to its heart, where the Prism Drake sleeps, and Pip can draw you a map of every level. New monsters live down there and on Starfall Isle, and a few can mend themselves once a fight.
Every cave has a map of its own: tap the minimap to see what you've explored.
Quests are numbered and marked with a gold star, and the Quests page can search, sort and filter them.
Tidier Character and Companions screens, no more bulging foreheads seen from the side, bearded dwarves show their mouths, and recoloured monsters and characters take their new colour all over.
Robes, chain mail, capes, festive hats and masks are redrawn to fit every hero, weapons in hand look crisp, Christmas brings striped scarves, and What's new sums up each big update in a few lines.

releases.title: Villages and gear you can see
notes: Every land has a village now, with 75 new quests from level 2 to 195, a treasure at the end of each village's story and dozens of villagers to meet.
Starfall Isle has a fairy village, Glimmerbough, and under it the Glimmerdeep, a cave of singing crystal. The Fallen Star and the Prism Drake are new bosses.
Level 200 is the top: Elder Oak's last quests earn the Goldleaf gear, and your name shines gold.
Gloves, boots and necklaces show on your hero, and armour comes in nine colour tiers from Copper to Topaz, a set for every guild.
Festive seasons: Halloween, Christmas, the New Year and Easter each bring treats and a hat for your new head slot.

releases.title: Starfall Isle
notes: Sail from Sneezle Sands to Starfall Isle, a new island where a star fell long ago, once Captain Brine's ship is ready.
Quests can ask you to bring things: monsters drop them, chests hold them, and some you carve or piece together yourself.
Status capes: beat every monster in a land, or finish a whole collection, and Orla the Weaver makes you a cape to wear.
Adventurers travel in groups. They can turn down your invite, let you join their party, and move on after a while.
Caves open into rocky hills, music fades from land to land, and frost monsters live in the cold north.

releases.title: One continent
notes: The lands are one world now: walk anywhere on the continent with no loading screen and no stop at a border, the ground, music, weather and monsters changing as you go.
Lands load in moments, and you can walk on into the next before it has finished.
Roads fade from one land's look into the next and are lined here and there with fences, walls, hedges or lanterns.
Treasure chests fill up again after a while, with gold and something new.
The coast slopes down into a sea that's paler in the shallows.

releases.title: A world of shapes
notes: The lands lie side by side as one continent, each with a shape of its own: snow and ice in the north, deserts and beaches in the south.
Walk over a border anywhere. A fence, rocks or a city wall stands where a quest still keeps the way closed.
Tap the minimap for the world map: the whole continent as it really looks, to drag about and zoom.
Rivers run from their springs to the sea or into a lake, and the land slopes down to the shore.
Towns sit in countryside of their own, and Prismhaven and Ingothold are walled in stone.

releases.title: Hills, mountains and rivers
notes: Every land has hills, and some have mountains: climb them anywhere, and look for the chests and bosses on the summits.
Lakes and rivers with bridges and jetties, and footpaths winding across the fields.
The sun crosses the sky, and shadows turn and stretch with the time of day.
People live out in the lands with stories of their own, and the minimap shows who's who.
Quests give treasures no monster drops, the Bag can be searched and sorted, and a gold arrow marks better gear.

releases.title: Something every day
notes: A gift each day you play, three daily bounties, titles to earn and rewards as the Monster Book fills.
Every monster has a card: collect them for Tilly the Toymaker, and give toys to your companions.
Seal Stones work on any monster at any HP, in five kinds up to the rainbow Wishing Seal.
Gloves, boots and necklaces have slots of their own, round your hero on the Character screen.
A calmer battle screen, one kind of window everywhere, richer sound and a How to play that plays the game.

releases.title: Welcome to Storyleaf
notes: The game is called Storyleaf now, with new names for its towns, lands and people.
Storyleaf speaks eleven languages, and the story at the start is told in animated pictures.
Day and night and changing weather, and your wounds stay with you between fights.
Every skill has a look of its own, new spells raise and lower stats, and friends think before they act.
Faster fights with 2× and Auto, gear dropped by monsters, Homeward Feathers and backups to Files.

releases.title: Bosses with a story
notes: Bosses fight in waves, and tell a short story when you beat them.
Parties of five, companions that take orders, poison and curses, and dark caves lit only by your light.
Play several heroes, each with a save of their own.
Trade with adventurers, sell to shops, and keep a Monster Book of everything you meet.
A livelier world: candy Gumdrop Peaks, little animals and birds, and adventurers dressed for their level.

releases.title: A bigger Storyleaf
notes: The world grows to 30 maps, with a world atlas, winding roads, caves, snowfall, icy ponds and busier towns.
Every item and skill has its own art, magic weapons glow, and blacksmiths forge gear from monster materials.
A storybook soundtrack, new sound effects with volume settings, an intro for new heroes and a What's new list.

releases.title: First steps into Storyleaf
notes: 14 maps joined by winding roads: Meadowbrook, Prismhaven and Ingothold, plus wild zones from Sunny Meadow to Moonwhisper.
Random encounters and turn-based battles fought where you stand. Big spells splash onto nearby monsters.
81 monsters across seven elements, with rare colour variants and three bosses.
Capture with Seal Stones and keep up to 5 companions. Your first hatches from the starter egg.
Quests, shops, healers, checkpoints, an in-game calendar and a chiptune soundtrack.
